title: Guidance Watermarking for Diffusion Models
claim: Any off-the-shelf detector's gradients, aggregated over image transformations, can steer the diffusion process to embed a watermark during generation.
layout: 3 colored panels: guidance on top, generation and detection below, arrows between
description: A system diagram in three rounded, color-coded boxes. The top red box, labeled 'Guidance process', runs left to right: latent z0, then a VAE trapezoid, then a decoded landscape image. Next come a 'Transform set T' box, a stack of augmented images, and a 'Detector φ' box. The detector outputs a bracketed list Loss1…Lossn, which leads to stacked noise-like gradient images labeled ∇z0 Loss_i. The bottom-left blue box, 'Watermarked Image Generation', shows the chain z_t → z_{t-1,w} → (dashed) z_{0w} → VAE → watermarked image. An upward arrow labeled 'Finish diffusion' links z_t to z0. A long 'Aggregation' arrow links the gradients back to z_{t-1,w}. The bottom-right green box, 'Detection', has a Detector φ box that outputs bit accuracy and P_FA. The eye goes first to the red top row.
caption: System-level diagram of the proposed guidance-based watermarking method.
abstract: This paper introduces a novel watermarking method for diffusion models. It is based on guiding the diffusion process using the gradient computed from any off-the-shelf watermark decoder. The gradient computation encompasses different image augmentations, increasing robustness to attacks against which the decoder was not originally robust, without retraining or fine-tuning. Our method effectively convert any \textit{post-hoc} watermarking scheme into an in-generation embedding along the diffusion process. We show that this approach is complementary to watermarking techniques modifying the variational autoencoder at the end of the diffusion process. We validate the methods on different diffusion models and detectors. The watermarking guidance does not significantly alter the generated image for a given seed and prompt, preserving both the diversity and quality of generation.
